ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two triangles. On the left is triangle NDG, ND is the upper horizontal side, DG is the vertical side, NG is the hypotenuse, and angle N is labeled 36°. On the right is triangle LGD, DG is still the vertical side, GL is the lower horizontal side, DL is the hypotenuse, there is a right-angle mark at G, and at D between DG and DL is labeled x°. Reasoning: It is known that ΔNDG ≅ ΔLGD. According to the vertex order of congruence, N ↔ L, D ↔ G, G ↔ D. In the figure, ∠G of the right triangle LGD = 90°, so the corresponding ∠D of the left triangle NDG = 90°. In ΔNDG, ∠N = 36°, ∠D = 90°, therefore ∠G = 180° − 36° − 90° = 54°. Also because ∠G in ΔNDG corresponds to ∠D in ΔLGD, and x is exactly ∠D of ΔLGD, so x = 54.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: triangle NDG is on the left with angle N marked 36°, segment ND horizontal, and segment DG vertical; triangle LGD is on the right with a right-angle marker at G and the unknown angle x marked at D between DG and DL. Because the right triangle LGD has ∠G = 90°, the corresponding angle ∠D in triangle NDG is also 90°. In triangle NDG, compute ∠G = 180° − 36° − 90° = 54°. Since ∠G in ΔNDG corresponds to ∠D in ΔLGD, x = 54.
